value.title: Multiletter Marton achievability

value.title: Marginal-balance and correlation necessities for a two-letter Marton gain
value.summary:
Accepted statement:

For the governed half-skew BSSC product channel P^{otimes 2}, let M be the unnormalized finite-auxiliary Marton sum value of any law (W,U,V)-X_1X_2-(Y^2,Z^2), let q_i=Pr[X_i=1], Q=q_1+q_2, let C_out=I(Y_1;Y_2)+I(Z_1;Z_2), and let c_in=P(X_1X_2=11)-q_1q_2. Canonical transaction 33a5944dca980bf94cc869c6c7dee2d04385ff58 supplies the two pre-averaging Marton-to-input rows and their universal average M <= G(P_{X_1X_2})+2r, while canonical transaction 88a1004f309460f3ec1cacdae88d30f88559f9bc supplies the exact directed threshold T=2L_RTD. The exact identity G=F(q_1)+F(q_2)-C_out/2 and the coordinatewise concave row envelopes imply that M>T forces q_1,q_2 in (3/8,5/8), hence in (7/20,13/20), together with 17/20<Q<23/20, C_out<7/160=0.04375<0.044 bits, and |c_in|<7/40. On the reflected/transposed family P(00)=P(11)=alpha and P(01)=P(10)=1/2-alpha, a gain additionally forces 1/8<alpha<5/13. These are necessary conditions only; they do not establish a two-letter gain, rule one out, or give a capacity converse.

Scope qualifications (verbatim):
- Applies to the governed half-skew BSSC product channel P^{otimes 2}.
- Applies to the unnormalized finite-auxiliary Marton sum value.
- The conclusions are necessary conditions conditional on M>T.
- It neither constructs nor proves a two-letter gain.
- It does not rule out a two-letter gain.
- It is not a capacity converse.
- From the threshold reference, only the unconditional RTD calculus and interval certificate are needed; neither (H-Marton) nor (H-binary) is used.

value.title: Output-correlation decomposition and concave-envelope pruning proof
value.summary: Proof used to establish the linked accepted claim. It combines the required Marton-to-input rows with the exact decomposition of the averaged product-channel input mutual information into two coordinate terms minus one half of the within-receiver output correlation. Coordinatewise and sum-marginal concave envelopes, together with the required directed threshold, give the accepted marginal restrictions and output-correlation bound. The affine BSSC output laws and a Pinsker argument give the accepted input-covariance bound, while monotonicity on the reflected/transposed one-parameter family gives the stated alpha window. This proof item establishes only the necessary conditions in the linked claim.

value.title: Directed marginal and output-correlation pruning audit
value.summary: Tool used for the computationally audited portion of the linked accepted claim. Using exact rational checks and outward-rounded standard-library decimal intervals, it reconstructs the required directed RTD threshold and verifies the coordinate, correlation, covariance, sum-marginal, and reflected-family endpoint comparisons supporting the accepted rational cutoffs. It does not replace the analytic information-theoretic identities, concavity arguments, or Pinsker derivation and does not establish a gain, a no-gain theorem, or a capacity converse.

placementAudits.rationale: The accepted claim gives structural necessary conditions for candidate two-letter finite-auxiliary Marton improvements, placing it directly in the existing multiletter Marton achievability program and its dedicated marginal-correlation pruning thread.
